question: Why are the cane toads at the front of their spread across Australia faster than those behind?
answer: Because the fastest keep breeding with the fastest. The farthest travellers reach new ground first and mate with each other. Phillips and colleagues found front-line toads had longer legs, and the invasion sped up from about 10 km a year to over 50. Speed was sorted to the edge, not won by surviving better.
move: At the edge of anything spreading, expect the most extreme to gather.
ask: Am I judging a whole group by the boldest few who happened to reach me first?
reference: Phillips, Brown, Webb & Shine, Invasion and the evolution of speed in toads, Nature, 2006
